chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur Buzurg, from Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: A man from your mawali married a woman, then divorced her, and she became independent of him. He wanted to remarry her, but she refused him except that he make a vow to God that he would not divorce her and would not marry another woman over her. He gave her that, then it occurred to him to marry another woman after that. So what should he do?

He said: Bad is what he did, and he did not know what would occur in his heart by night and by day. Tell him to fulfill the condition for the woman, for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The believers are upon their conditions.'

So the way in this narration is one of two things: One is that it is to be understood as recommending (mustahabb), because whoever rules according to what the narration entails, it is recommended for him to fulfill the condition that his tongue offered, even if it is not obligatory. And the other way is that it is to be understood as based on taqiyya (dissimulation), because those who differ from us would obligate this condition and make him sinful if he violates it, and that which confirms the first narrations.

key_terms.المُؤمِنُونَ عِندَ شُرُوطِهِم: The believers are upon their conditions
key_terms.يَجعَلَ لِلّهِ عَلَيهِ: He makes a vow to God
key_terms.يُرَاجِعَهَا: He wants to remarry her (revive the marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband vows to God not to divorce his wife or marry another, but later wants to?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in the context of marital conditions (shurut), where the Imam validates the wife's stipulation that the husband not remarry, linking it to the Prophetic principle that 'believers are upon their conditions.' The scholar provides a nuanced jurisprudential analysis, suggesting the obligation is either recommended (mustahabb) due to the husband's voluntary vow, or obligatory (wajib) based on taqiyya to align with schools that enforce such conditions, thereby ensuring the husband's fidelity to his word.
